metadata.note: The Ashuelot Railroad ran from Keene, NH down the Ashuelot River valley through Swanzey, West Swanzey, Westport, Winchester and Ashuelot to Hinsdale and on to South Vernon, VT (23 3/4 mi, Foster), where it met the Connecticut River Railroad and the Vermont and Massachusetts. It never ran to Brattleboro. The Ashuelot company does not appear to have run its own trains in any well-established era, so the features are split by operator (Rule 4): Connecticut River Railroad 1851-1860, Cheshire Railroad 1861-1877 (operator uncertain), Connecticut River Railroad 1877-1892, Boston and Maine 1893-1952 as the Ashuelot Branch. From c.1912-13 the B&M's Fort Hill line made Dole Junction - South Vernon part of its Connecticut River main line, and branch trains started at Dole Junction; the B&M-era stub to South Vernon is drawn only to 1906 [OPEN]. Passenger service ended 5 Jan 1952 (Foster); freight ran until 1983 and the grade is now the Ashuelot Rail Trail. The Dole Junction - Fort Hill - Brattleboro line is B&M Connecticut River main line, not this road, and is not drawn here.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules eff. 30 Sept 1951), Boston and Maine Table 20 (Keene - Hinsdale - Dole Junction / Brattleboro); index entry 'Hinsdale, N.H., Bost.& Me., 20'
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. The Ashuelot grade is tagged old_railway_operator=B&M in OSM (railway=abandoned ways, most of them the Ashuelot Rail Trail cycleway/path); the whole Keene - Dole Junction trace ran on B&M-tagged ways (opstrace: 21.6 mi 'B&M', 0 mi on any other operator, no straight legs). South of Dole Junction the abandoned B&M-tagged grade (OSM way 171157978 and two short fragments) is followed to South Vernon, then ~0.3 mi of New England Central (ex-Central Vermont) track to the junction with the B&M Connecticut River Main Line. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the corridor and returned nothing. Waypoints: Keene depot site, West Swanzey, Westport, Winchester, Ashuelot, Hinsdale (Nominatim; Winchester and Hinsdale came back as township 'administrative' points and West Swanzey as a census place, so those were hand-pinned to the villages), Dole Junction (OSM railway=junction node) and South Vernon (OSM hamlet node). Each waypoint is within 0.3 km of the drawn line except South Vernon's hamlet node (1.1 km from the end of the continuous trace before gap-bridging; the drawn line ends at the B&M/NECR junction 0.4 km south-east of it).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] B&M Dole Junction - South Vernon stub: drawn 1893-1906, 1906 being the last confirmed year (B&M 1906 station list), not a known end; the c.1912-13 Fort Hill line probably ended branch running to South Vernon (1912 bridge per TrailLink vs 1913 per Wikipedia). (2) Operator 1861-1877: Cheshire lease dated 1860 (de.Wiki Ashuelot), 11 Feb 1861 to 1865 (court-opinion summary, text unread), or 1872-1877 (de.Wiki Cheshire); who ran trains 1865-1872 is not established - drawn as Cheshire with medium-low confidence. (3) Passenger end 1952 rests on Foster alone; fallback is 1951 from the Official Guide. (4) Opening Dec 1850 (Foster) vs 1851 (Griffin, de.Wiki) - drawn from 1851. (5) Headways for 1851-1950 are wholly unsourced; a B&M public timetable of 1914/1921/1932 would settle frequency and whether through cars ran on to East Northfield (Foster's 1952 wording implies they did). (6) A B&M Connecticut River main line layer (East Northfield - South Vernon - Dole Jct - Fort Hill - Brattleboro) does not exist in data/; that is a separate gap.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.rewrite_audit: 2026-10-15: layer rewritten from research/branches/ashuelot_railroad.txt. Corrected: passenger end 1955 -> 1952 (5 Jan 1952 last passenger motor car, Foster; the old 1955 was an unsourced approximation and its '1983' was the freight end); start 1850 -> 1851 (source conflict collapsed to the later year); the single 'Ashuelot Railroad' feature in one colour split by operator under Rule 4 (Connecticut River Railroad, Cheshire Railroad, Boston and Maine, with B&M years now in the B&M colour; the 1890 Ashuelot-CRR merger is no longer a segment boundary); geometry no longer doubles back from Dole Junction to Brattleboro over the Fort Hill line (B&M main line, ~9 mi) and now includes the missing Dole Junction - South Vernon leg (pre-c.1912 terminal); 1951 frequency corrected to one mixed train a day (headway 1440) from the Official Guide; label 'Keene – Brattleboro' replaced; geometry_quality added.

properties.geometry_quality: Keene - South Vernon: traced 23.9 mi against a documented 23 3/4 mi (Foster p.396) / 24.0 mi (Official Guide 1951 Table 20 Keene - Dole Jct 21.8 mi + Fowler Vermont list Dole Jct - South Vernon 2.2 mi). Keene - Dole Junction part traced 21.6 mi against 21.8 mi. Approximated (straight) legs, all on the Dole Junction - South Vernon stretch, bridging disconnected OSM fragments of the abandoned grade: 0.16 mi at 42.737 N, 0.23 mi at 42.733 N, and 0.12 mi joining the grade to the NECR track at 42.730 N - about 0.51 mi in all. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. as it stood at abandonment (1983); 1850s-1880s alignment differences, the Keene in-town approach (the line starts at the south end of the rail-trail, ~0.3 km from the Main Street / Railroad Street depot site, which was not separately located), and the c.1912-13 rebuilding of the South Vernon end when Dole Junction - South Vernon became B&M Connecticut River main line are not drawn. The last ~0.3 mi at South Vernon uses present-day NECR (ex-Central Vermont) track, a later layout than the era drawn.

segments.note: The Ashuelot Railroad (Keene - Swanzey - West Swanzey - Westport - Winchester - Ashuelot - Hinsdale - South Vernon, VT) was worked from opening by the Connecticut River Railroad as lessee, on a 10-year lease at $30,000 a year (Foster p.396; de.Wiki: lease dated 7 Dec 1849). Opening year conflict: Foster gives first trains 9 Dec 1850; Griffin (1904) p.448 says the road was built in 1850 and 'trains began to run in 1851'; de.Wiki also opens it in 1851 - drawn from 1851, the later date. End 1860 is the lease-change year (Cheshire lease 1860 per de.Wiki, or 11 Feb 1861 per a court-opinion summary): an operator boundary, not a break in service. Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: start year from Griffin, History of the Town of Keene (1904) p.448 and de.Wikipedia 'Ashuelot Railroad' (Foster p.396 gives Dec 1850 - conflict recorded); CRR lessee and lease term from Foster p.396 and de.Wikipedia; end year = lease change per de.Wikipedia. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Second Connecticut River Railroad era: after the Ashuelot company's bankruptcy a new Ashuelot Railroad Company was formed on 21 April 1877 and leased to the CRR the same day (de.Wiki; en.Wiki CRR 'acquired in 1877'). The 7 Feb 1890 merger of the Ashuelot into the CRR (Nashua City Station) did not change who ran the trains, so it is not a split here. Ends 1892: the Boston and Maine leased the CRR from 1 January 1893 (Foster p.401; en.Wiki). Foster p.401 records the Ashuelot company building a new engine house on Main Street, Keene, in 1885. Nothing is drawn in CRR colour for 1861-1876. Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: start 21 Apr 1877 from de.Wikipedia 'Ashuelot Railroad' and en.Wikipedia 'Connecticut River Railroad'; 1890 merger from Nashua City Station; end = B&M lease of 1 Jan 1893 per Foster p.401 and en.Wikipedia. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Cheshire Railroad lease era of the Ashuelot Railroad. OPERATOR CONFIDENCE MEDIUM-LOW: de.Wiki (Ashuelot) has the Cheshire leasing and operating the line 1860-1877; a CourtListener summary of Ashuelot Railroad v. Cheshire Railroad dates the lease 11 Feb 1861 'for a term running until 1865' (opinion text not retrieved); de.Wiki (Cheshire) gives the Cheshire lease only from 1872 to 21 April 1877. So 1861-1865 and 1872-1877 each have two sources, while 1865-1872 rests on de.Wiki (Ashuelot) alone - the Ashuelot company may have worked its own trains for part of that time. Start collapsed to 1861; ends 21 April 1877 when the reorganised Ashuelot company was leased to the Connecticut River Railroad (shared boundary year with the CRR feature). Passenger service ran throughout - the dispute is over who ran it, not whether it ran. Headway is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the operator and both boundaries come from de.Wikipedia (Ashuelot and Cheshire articles) and search-result summaries of two court opinions whose text was not read; nothing has checked passenger service itself or the headway for these years.
CourtListener opinions 3572203 and 8087835 (Ashuelot Railroad v. Cheshire Railroad; titles and search summaries only)

segments.note: Boston and Maine Ashuelot Branch, Keene - Dole Junction (Connecticut & Passumpsic Division in the 1906/1914 B&M station lists, Fitchburg Division in the 1930/1941 employee timetables). The B&M ran it from its 1 Jan 1893 lease of the Connecticut River Railroad (Foster p.401); the 1919 CRR merger is not a split. Until c.1912-13 the branch ran on to South Vernon, VT - see the separate stub feature; drawn from Keene to Dole Junction for the whole B&M era. A 1948 photograph shows a B&M Ashuelot Branch train at Hinsdale. The 1906/1914/1930/1941 lists are employee/accounting documents, not passenger proof on their own. Headway is an estimate: no pre-1951 public timetable for the branch was consulted (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: start = B&M lease of the CRR, 1 Jan 1893 (Foster p.401; en.Wikipedia); 1948 train photographed at Hinsdale (Beverly Historical Society); branch named in B&M lists of 1906, 1914, 1930, 1941 (Nashua City Station). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Last years. The Sept 1951 Official Guide (Table 20, reprinted in the Feb 1952 issue) shows ONE mixed train each way daily on the branch: northbound Dole Jct about 8:15 AM - Hinsdale - Ashuelot - Westport - West Swanzey - Keene 9:55; southbound Keene 10:30 - Dole Junction 11:50 AM. The table's other columns are B&M buses Keene - Hinsdale - Brattleboro, not trains. Ends 1952: Foster (a B&M Keene ticket clerk 1917-57) records that 'January 5, 1952 saw the last gasoline passenger motor car operated on the Ashuelot Branch from Keene to East Northfield, Mass.' - read as the end of passenger service; single source. If Foster is rejected the confirmed end falls back to 1951. Freight continued (B&M, then the Green Mountain Railroad as lessee c.1982-83) until the line closed in 1983; it is now the Ashuelot Rail Trail.
sources: Segment-level: 1951 service and frequency from the Official Guide Table 20 (eff. 30 Sept 1951); 5 Jan 1952 last passenger run from Foster pp.401-402. Day-of-week pattern of the mixed train not legible in the OCR.

segments.note: [OPEN] The Ashuelot's original south end, Dole Junction - South Vernon, VT (2.2 mi), in the B&M years. The B&M station list of 1 Jan 1906 still defines the Ashuelot Branch as 'South Vernon to Keene'; the 1914 list and later ones say 'Dole Junction to Keene', after the B&M's Fort Hill line (c.1912-13) made this stretch part of the Connecticut River main line. 1906 is the LAST CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when branch trains stopped running through to South Vernon (probably c.1912-13). Do not extend without evidence. No branch train is positively evidenced on this stub in B&M years; the 1906 list is an employee document. Headway is an estimate (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: Nashua City Station B&M agents-and-stations lists of 1906 ('South Vernon to Keene') and 1914 ('Dole Junction to Keene'); Fowler Vermont list line 1 for the South Vernon - Doolittle - Dole Jct sequence and mileposts. No timetable checked; headway not sourced.
